original_question: Let G be a connected graph with chromatic number k >= 2, let x be the principal eigenvector of its adjacency matrix, and let S be an independent set of vertices. Must the squared l2-mass on S always satisfy sum_{v in S} x_v^2 <= 1/2 - (k - 2)/sqrt((k - 2)^2 + 4(k - 1)(n - k + 1))?
target_in_paper: Section 20, Conjecture 23 (Gregory, cf. Cioabă) on principal eigenvectors of graphs. In the survey it is presented immediately after Theorem 5, which states the bipartite case and motivates this chromatic-number extension. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right topic and most of the right objects: a connected graph, chromatic number k>=2, the principal eigenvector of the adjacency matrix, an independent set S, and the question of whether the squared l2-mass of that eigenvector on S is universally bounded above by a function of n and k. That matches the intent of Gregory’s conjecture as recorded in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
missing_details: The paper’s statement is for a connected graph G of order n, so n must be defined explicitly as n=|V(G)|; your draft uses n in the bound without defining it. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S009589562500070X?utm_source=openai))

The principal eigenvector is not just any eigenvector: in the surrounding context it is the unique unit positive eigenvector x=(x_v)_{v in V(G)} of the real adjacency matrix A(G) corresponding to the spectral radius lambda(G). The unit normalization ||x||_2=1 is implicit in the paper and should be made explicit in a stand-alone question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
S should be stated as a subset of V(G) that is an independent set of G. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

The inequality in your draft is missing a factor 2 in the denominator of the second term. The paper’s bound is 1/2 - (k-2)/(2*sqrt((k-2)^2 + 4(k-1)(n-k+1))). ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S009589562500070X?utm_source=openai))

The quantifier should be fully explicit: the conjecture asks whether the inequality holds for every connected n-vertex graph G with chi(G)=k>=2 and every independent set S. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
For a stand-alone formulation, it helps to name chi(G)=k and A(G) explicitly, so that no notation is imported implicitly from the surrounding section. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
refined_question: For every connected graph G of order n with chromatic number chi(G)=k>=2, if x=(x_v)_{v in V(G)} is the unit positive eigenvector of the adjacency matrix A(G) corresponding to the spectral radius lambda(G), and S is an independent set in G, must one always have sum_{v in S} x_v^2 <= 1/2 - (k-2)/(2*sqrt((k-2)^2 + 4(k-1)(n-k+1)))? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful stand-alone version of the draft. The survey’s Section 20 first defines the principal eigenvector for connected graphs via Perron-Frobenius, then states Cioabă’s Theorem 5 for the bipartite case, and then records Gregory’s chromatic-number generalization as Conjecture 23. I kept exactly that scope, added only the implicit notation needed for self-containment, and corrected the missing factor 2 in the bound so that the question matches the conjecture as stated in the literature quoted by the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
